newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude weak as prompt supply piles up.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude weak as prompt supply piles up.

text.p: North Sea crude prices were weak on Wednesday as supply piled up after recent high prices prevented cargoes leaving the area, traders said.
Offshore loaded Norwegian crude was the worst hit, they added, because freight rates had fallen and left a swathe of costly Statfjord and Gullfaks cargoes.
The weakness spread well into the second decade, with a Nov 14 loading Forties cargo sold at Dated Brent +8 cents, seven cents below Tuesday.
"The panic just hasn't hit the back end yet," a trader said.
Oseberg was an exception with a 32 cent premium to Dated.
IPE December Brent fell 23 cents to $23.51 per barrel by 1824 GMT. The Dec/Jan spread eased by about five cents to +38 cents.
Dated Brent traded at a steady Dec Brent -35 cents for a 12-14 loader, and traders said at that price U.S. refiners might begin to look at the grade
West African crude differentials were also on the verge of a sharp fall, although the lack of activity made valuation obscure.
A U.S. oil company trader valued Qua Iboe at no better than Dated Brent +55 cents.
The only reported activity was a Qua Iboe sold into a Senegalese tender for Nov 15-20 arrival. Escravos had also been offered into the tender but was rejected.
Traders said there were very few distressed cargoes but West African crude needed to move out of the market to prevent further falls in differentials.
"I think it will trade lower because crude needs to move out of the region. It is not going to the US and some players may try to force the arb to the Far East to work," the trader said.
